newsitem.title: POLAND: CIB values Polish KGHM at $1.0-1.3 bln - paper.
newsitem.headline: CIB values Polish KGHM at $1.0-1.3 bln - paper.

text.p: Copper concern KGHM Polska Miedz SA, due for flotation in early July, is worth between $1.0 and $1.3 billion, a Creditanstalt Investment Bank (CIB) report carried by the Rzeczpospolita business daily on Thursday said.
Earlier this week Merrill Lynch said the Polish copper giant was worth between $1.1 and $1.3 billion.
CIB forecast KGHM's production costs to be reduced to $1,670 per tonne by the year 2000 from $1,950 now. Merrill expected costs to fall to $1,435 per tonne in the year 2000.
CIB said KGHM's copper-ore deposits would be able to sustain full production until 2015.
CIB said that KGHM planned to invest 1.008 billion zlotys this year, including investing 582 million in core production and 77 million in its mobile telephone affiliate Polkomtel.
In 1998, KGHM will invest 858 million zlotys, with some 715 million in core-activities and 58 million in Polkomtel.
CIB said KGHM will invest 657 million zlotys in 1999, including 550 on production, and 451 million in 2000, with 401 million of it spent on core-activities.
It said the scope of the planned investment would mean that KGHM would need outside sources of financing.
